resolvedFindings.resolution: Request must match verified session/owner/device/manualCode; scoped reads reuse the existing device endpoint, and old Backend responses remain strictly checked.
Success/catch paths verify context and binding generation; identity plus verification share a five-second deadline with absolute wall-clock confirmation.
Identity is bounded; after-await/catch paths verify generation; old finally cannot clear a newer generation owner.
Merged one-shot pending probes exclude their just-settled request ID and do not create a zero-delay retry chain.
Ordinary and shortcut cleanup release their captured owner token, so late cleanup cannot release a later written lease.
Requested work at least sixty seconds old is locally expired using the server envelope timestamp, preventing replay after reconnect or cache rotation.

Recent attempted outcomes now use the stable device/manualCode/requestId identity, while in-flight entries retain binding/generation ownership. Cancellation during capture or upload writes the stable recent outcome synchronously before recovery can enqueue the same request in a new generation. Requests cancelled before capture remain eligible for explicit rediscovery, and fresh request IDs continue normally.

Written lifecycle calls retain a native-read-in-flight flag until desktopCapturer.getSources actually settles, independently of the processor timeout and capture lease. An explicit retry while native work remains pending returns a clear failure without issuing another native read; only the call owning that flag clears it in finally. Late native results retain signal and owner fencing, and later work can read sources once the original native operation ends.

reviewChecks: A fresh same-session request is admitted with device credentials and optional sessionId/requestId, without web-login token.
Missing or mismatched owner/session/device/code is rejected; non-live, mock, stale or changed bindings cannot authorize capture.
Cancelled/processing/completed/failed work does not capture; request state is checked before and after native capture.
Late native/upload/report results cannot upload old images, notify replacement work or release a newer lock.
Unknown uploads are not blindly retried, and cancelled-request terminal 409 is not attributed to replacement work.
Old recovery rejection, expired context or overdue five-second response does not reopen delivery or release a current lease.
A pending canonical request matching the just-settled ID is not re-enqueued and produces no continuous extra polling.
Old loop identity resolve/reject after stop cannot open a stream or launch fallback; old finally preserves new owner.
Written awake protection is renewable, bounded and released on invalid binding, stop/suspend/quit; no display lock or audio start.
Ordinary branch remains selected outside written mode; its reviewed cleanup change is owner fencing only.
Backend scoped reads enforce current binding/request ownership, preserve terminal states and legacy behavior, and create no task/model/billing mutation.
Server clock rejects old work with a slow local clock and admits fresh work with an eight-hour-fast local clock.

A capture/upload attempt cancelled on binding loss is not recaptured or reuploaded when the same binding/request returns with a new generation; a different explicit request continues, and a request never captured may be rediscovered after cancellation.

An unabortable written native source read is issued once: explicit retry while pending makes no second native call, its old late result cannot release a newer lock, and native reading resumes only after actual native settlement. The guard applies only to written lifecycle calls, preserving the ordinary branch.
